I am a 65-year-old farmer from Quzhou County, on the North China Plain in southern Hebei. I have farmed this land for over 40 years, and I went to technical secondary school in my youth — back then, that was quite something for a village boy. I know every mu of my 8 mu of good flat land, and I know what this soil can do.

It is now early spring, and my winter wheat is already in the ground, greening up after the winter dormancy. In Quzhou, we follow the wheat-corn double-cropping system that our grandfathers' grandfathers followed, but with modern seeds and techniques. I will not gamble with new crops like sweet potatoes or soybeans on my main fields — the market is steady for wheat and corn, the buyers come right to the village, and I know the inputs and the risks inside out.

For this year, my plan is simple and proven: all 8 mu will stay in the winter wheat rotation, and after the June harvest, I will immediately plant summer corn on the same 8 mu. I use improved wheat varieties and hybrid corn seeds — they cost more, but the yield gain pays for itself. I will apply fertilizer based on soil testing I did last autumn: roughly 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu for the wheat; for the corn, I will push nitrogen to 20 kg per mu because corn is a hungry crop, with similar P and K. 

Water is everything here on the plain. For wheat, I will irrigate four times: green-up in March, jointing in April, heading in May, and one more at filling if the weather turns dry. For corn, three irrigations: right after sowing, at the big trumpet stage, and at filling. I keep my old diesel pump maintained myself — learned that in school. Pesticides are necessary with the pests we get now, but I use them sparingly: twice on wheat (one for aphids, one for rust if needed), and twice on corn (herbicide at sowing, one insecticide later). I use rotary tillage before wheat planting and before corn sowing; it preserves moisture and is gentler on the soil structure than deep ploughing, which matters because we plant two crops a year on the same ground.

I expect about 550 kg per mu of wheat and 650 kg per mu of corn. Not the highest in the county, but consistent, and consistency is how you survive as a farmer my age. I do not take risks I cannot recover from.
